headline: TLS certificate compression is off by default, the archive readers name every entry as other tools extract it, and the first compromised-key check per curve takes milliseconds
summary:
TLS certificate compression (RFC 8879) is now off unless an option lists algorithms. With compression on, OpenSSL decompresses the peer's certificate during the handshake, before the chain is verified, so a client or an on-path attacker could reach the decompressor before authentication.

`b.archive.read.tar` applies GNU long-name and long-link records and reads every other header record GNU tar and bsdtar use to name or size an entry, and refuses an archive where the two tools read a header differently. `b.archive.read.zip` `inspect()` checks every local header against the central directory, and entries are named as unzip, 7-Zip and bsdtar extract them. `b.guardArchive.validateEntries` checks every path segment and every name a reader may extract an entry under.

The first `b.crypto.compromisedKey` check on each curve builds its small-scalar table by point addition, so `b.pqcAgent.create({ ca: tls.rootCertificates })` no longer spends over a second at startup.

items.title: TLS certificate compression is off by default
items.body: Listeners from `b.router` `listen()`, `b.mail.server.tls.context`, the `sniCallback` context of `b.cert.create`, and connections from `b.httpClient`, `b.pqcAgent.create`, `b.wsClient.connect`, `b.network.tls.ocsp.connect`, `requireStapled`, `requireGood`, `b.network.tls.applyToContext`, `b.network.tls.buildOptions` and `b.network.tls.outboundPosture()` advertise no compression algorithm unless the caller passes `certificateCompression`. With compression on, OpenSSL decompresses the peer's `Certificate` message before the chain is verified: a listener with `requestCert` decompresses any client's certificate, and a dial decompresses whatever certificate the server or anyone on the path sends. To keep compressed certificates, pass `certificateCompression` with names from `b.network.tls.certificateCompressionAlgorithms()`.

items.title: `certificateCompression` is checked wherever it is accepted
items.body: `b.httpClient.request` and `b.httpClient.configurePool` accept `certificateCompression`; a request's list overrides the pool's, `[]` turns compression off, and a request whose list differs from the pool's opens its own connection. A non-empty list on an https request that goes through `opts.agent` or a `b.network.proxy` tunnel rejects with `http-client/bad-opts`. A list that is not an array, holds an entry that is not a string, names an algorithm the runtime does not support, or names one twice is refused when the option is passed, with `tls/bad-cert-compression` (`network-tls/bad-tls-options` from `b.network.tls.buildOptions`); a duplicate used to fail later inside OpenSSL with `ERR_CRYPTO_OPERATION_FAILED`. `b.network.tls.ocsp.connect`, `requireStapled` and `requireGood` check the list before they dial, and refuse `brotli` with `tls/unsafe-cert-compression` on a runtime whose Brotli decoder is unfixed.

items.title: A shared Brotli library is checked by its own version
items.body: On a Node built against a shared Brotli library (`process.config.variables.node_shared_brotli`), `brotli` counts as unfixed when `process.versions.brotli` is below 1.2.1 or does not parse. On such a build `b.constants.TLS_CERT_COMPRESSION()` leaves it out, an explicit list naming it is refused with `tls/unsafe-cert-compression`, and `b.safeDecompress` refuses `algorithm: "brotli"` with `safe-decompress/unsafe-runtime`. The messages name the shared library and ask for Brotli 1.2.1 or later when the Node release itself is fixed.

items.title: `b.archive.read.tar` applies GNU long-name and long-link records
items.body: A GNU `L` or `K` record now sets the name or link target of the entry after it, and is no longer returned as a `././@LongLink` entry, so `inspect()`, `extract()`, `extractEntries()` and the guard check before extraction see the name GNU tar and bsdtar write. An `L` or `K` body is read up to its first NUL and is refused with `archive-tar/entry-too-large` when it exceeds `bombPolicy.maxEntryDecompressedBytes` or 64 KiB. Solaris `X` headers are read like pax `x` headers, and a pax `GNU.sparse.name` names the entry ahead of `path`. Pax records are read by byte length, so archives that GNU tar `--format=posix` and bsdtar `--format=pax` write with non-ASCII names are listed and extracted under those names; earlier releases refused them with `archive-tar/bad-pax-record`.

items.title: `b.archive.read.tar` refuses headers that GNU tar and bsdtar read differently
items.body: The reader refuses: an empty or stacked `L` or `K` record (`archive-tar/bad-long-record`); an `L` or `K` value that differs from the pax `path`, `GNU.sparse.name` or `linkpath` (`archive-tar/long-name-pax-conflict`); a link target before an entry that is not a link (`archive-tar/link-target-on-non-link`); a pax header or `L`/`K` record with no entry after it or followed by a volume label (`V`) or Solaris ACL (`A`) header (`archive-tar/dangling-extended-header`); two pax `x` or `X` headers before one entry (`archive-tar/redundant-extended-header`); a pax global header carrying `path`, `linkpath`, `size`, `GNU.sparse.*`, `SCHILY.realsize` or `SUN.holesdata` (`archive-tar/global-entry-attribute`); a malformed pax record, or a pax key that is empty, starts with a space or tab, or contains a NUL (`archive-tar/bad-pax-record`); a NUL in a pax `path`, `linkpath` or `GNU.sparse.name` value, or an empty `linkpath` (`archive-tar/bad-pax-name`); a pax `size` that is empty or not plain decimal (`archive-tar/bad-pax-size`); a link, directory, device or FIFO entry with a nonzero size (`archive-tar/size-on-non-file`); a sparse header the tools read differently (`archive-tar/bad-sparse-header`); a name or link target that is not valid UTF-8, including under pax `hdrcharset=BINARY` (`archive-tar/name-not-utf8`); an octal field with bytes after its terminator (`archive-tar/bad-octal`); and a magic field other than `ustar\0` plus a version or the GNU `ustar  \0` (`archive-tar/bad-magic`), which includes V7-format archives. The reader stops at the first all-zero block, as both tools do.

items.title: `b.archive.read.tar` does not extract sparse files or uninterpreted entry types
items.body: `extract()` and `extractEntries()` refuse with `archive-tar/entry-type-refused`, under every `entryTypePolicy`: sparse files (`tar -S` in GNU or pax format, `SCHILY.realsize`, `SUN.holesdata`, or a GNU-format entry that sets a byte in the old sparse map, isextended or realsize fields), and volume label (`V`), Solaris ACL (`A`), multi-volume (`M`), old GNU long name (`N`) and other typeflags the reader does not interpret. `inspect()` lists them with `entryType: "unknown"`. A GNU `--label` archive is therefore listed but not extracted.

items.title: `b.archive.read.zip` `inspect()` checks local headers
items.body: `inspect()` and `entries()` run the local-header pass that `extract` and `extractEntries` run, and share it: every local header, directories included, must match its central directory entry in name bytes, method, CRC-32, sizes, data descriptor and general-purpose flag bits 0, 3, 6, 11 and 13 (`archive-read/lfh-cd-skew`), an offset without a local header throws `archive-read/bad-lfh-signature`, and a ZIP structure between entries throws `archive-read/embedded-archive`. The pass reads local headers in file order through 64 KiB windows, so the number of adapter reads follows the archive size rather than the entry count. `b.guardArchive.inspect` and `b.safeArchive.inspect` run the same checks, so an archive whose central directory lists `docs/readme.txt` while the local header names `../../evil.txt` is refused at inspect time.

items.title: `b.archive.read.zip` names entries as unzip, 7-Zip and bsdtar extract them
items.body: When a header carries an Info-ZIP Unicode Path extra field (0x7075) of version 1 whose CRC-32 matches the name field, the entry's name is that field's UTF-8 path; otherwise it is the name field. Default 7-Zip archives with non-ASCII names read under their UTF-8 names. A Unicode Path field that readers would interpret differently is refused with `archive-read/unicode-path-mismatch`, a name flagged UTF-8 that is not valid UTF-8 with `archive-read/bad-utf8-name`, and an unflagged name that is not valid UTF-8 is read as code page 437. When bit 11 is clear, each entry carries `altNames`, the code page 437 and UTF-8 decodes that Python's `zipfile` and Java read, and extraction refuses an entry when any of its names carries a critical issue.

items.title: `b.guardArchive.validateEntries` checks every path segment and every name
items.body: Path checks run on `name` and on every entry in an optional `altNames` array. Duplicate and case-collision checks compare every name of every entry, including each name's NFC form, its form with backslashes read as `/`, and its form with empty and `.` segments dropped, so `d\\a.txt`, `d/./a.txt`, `d//a.txt` and `./d/a.txt` next to `d/a.txt` are critical duplicates. Every path segment is checked: a trailing dot or leading or trailing whitespace draws `archive.filename.leading-trailing` (high), and a Windows reserved device name such as `a/CON` or `a/aux.c` draws `archive.filename.reserved-name` (critical), so `extractEntries()` refuses it as `b.safeArchive.extract` does. The new `reservedNamePolicy` option (`"reject"` in every profile) turns the device-name check to warn level with `"audit"` or off with `"allow"` for archives extracted only on Linux, such as a Linux kernel source tree. `b.guardArchive.inspect` passes every option other than `format`, `audit` and `signal` to `validateEntries`, checks them before reading the archive, and accepts `opts.signal`.

items.title: `b.archive.read.tar` reads base-256 numeric fields
items.body: Mode, uid, gid, size and mtime fields in base-256, which GNU tar and bsdtar write for an mtime before 1970 or after 2242, a uid or gid over 2097151, or a size of 8 GiB or more, are decoded; earlier releases refused them with `archive-tar/bad-octal`. A value outside its field's range is refused with `archive-tar/numeric-out-of-range`. A pax `mtime` record that is a decimal number of seconds sets the entry's mtime. The reader also accepts the magic-less volume label header that `tar --format=gnu --label` writes, reads GNU sparse extension blocks, and treats a regular entry whose name ends in `/` as a directory.

items.title: The first compromised-key check per curve takes milliseconds
items.body: `b.crypto.compromisedKey` builds its table of small-scalar public keys for P-256, P-384, P-521 and secp256k1 by point addition, with one scalar multiplication per curve instead of 255. It also skips the vendored `@blamejs/pki` key lint on a certificate whose key node and `@blamejs/pki` decode to the same SubjectPublicKeyInfo bytes. The first `b.pqcAgent.create({ ca: tls.rootCertificates })` in a process makes 3 scalar multiplications instead of 1530 and takes about 0.13 to 0.34 s instead of about 1.4 to 2.4 s on Node 26.12.1. `b.selfUpdate.standaloneVerifier.verify` builds its P-384 table from the published generator in about 4 to 6 ms instead of about 200 ms. The vendored `@blamejs/pki` 0.9.10 builds its own table the same way, so the paths where it checks keys itself (certificate, CSR and CRMF issuance, chain validation, trust anchors, and a compressed-point EC certificate passed as `ca`) no longer pay the cost either.

items.title: Vendored `@blamejs/pki` 0.9.10
items.body: `@blamejs/pki` moves from 0.9.9 to 0.9.10. Its first compromised-key check on each elliptic curve builds the small-scalar table by point addition, which takes a few milliseconds instead of up to about half a second.

items.title: `b.archive.tar` writes long non-ASCII names that other tools read
items.body: The builder counts pax record lengths and the ustar name and prefix fields in UTF-8 bytes. Before, a long name with non-ASCII characters produced a pax record whose length was wrong, or threw `archive-tar/field-overflow`.

items.title: `b.archive.read.zip` and `b.safeArchive.inspect` error codes
items.body: `b.safeArchive.inspect` refuses a `b.archive.adapters.trustedStream` source with `safe-archive/trusted-stream-unsupported`, the code `b.safeArchive.extract` throws, instead of `safe-archive/bad-source`.
